_comment: Tier-2 for skfem stokes#2, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1 / scipy 1.15.3. Claim (marked inherited, not empirically verified): enclosed-flow Stokes has a constant-pressure nullspace; pin one pressure DoF or add a mean-zero multiplier, and the signal is that spsolve RETURNS SUCCESSFULLY with the right velocity while the pressure carries an arbitrary additive constant. Ran: Taylor-Hood ElementVector(P2)/P1 on MeshTri().refined(3), 578 velocity and 81 pressure DOFs, lid-driven-cavity velocity prescribed on the whole boundary (so the flow is enclosed); the dense spectrum of the condensed block; the unpinned solve; and two pinned solves differing in WHICH DOF is pinned and at WHAT value. Printed: the nullspace is exactly one-dimensional and its vector is zero on the velocity block (2.795e-15) and constant on the pressure block (spread 6.543e-13). THE CLAIM IS CONFIRMED IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION: the unpinned solve raises nothing, warns NOTHING -- an empty catch_warnings record, no MatrixRankWarning -- and returns a finite vector whose velocity matches the pinned runs to 5.534e-14. That is worth setting beside hydraulic_resistance#2 and navier_stokes#3, which describe scipy emitting 'Matrix is exactly singular' on a singular block system: here the singular system is consistent, SuperLU returns a particular solution, and a guard built only on catching that warning does not fire. Pinning gives velocities agreeing to 5.539e-14 across both choices while the two pressures differ by an exact constant (spread 1.116e-11, offset -2.873724).
